sentences.en: This is 99% Invisible.
sentences.zh: 这里是《99%隐形》。

sentences.en: I'm Roman Mars.
sentences.zh: 我是罗曼·马尔斯。

sentences.en: The Chicago River used to be completely filthy.
sentences.zh: 芝加哥河曾经脏得一塌糊涂。

sentences.en: I mean, it's not great now, but it used to be so much worse.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，现在也好不到哪去，但过去要糟糕得多。

sentences.en: The people of Chicago were doing disgusting things to it.
sentences.zh: 芝加哥人当时对它做了些令人作呕的事。

sentences.en: Essentially using the river as a sewer and all of Chicago's waste, human waste,
sentences.zh: 基本上把这条河当成了下水道，把芝加哥所有的废物、人类排泄物，

sentences.en: and also as the stockyards grew up in the city,
sentences.zh: 还有随着城市发展而兴起的屠宰场，

sentences.en: all of the animal waste was dumped into the river.
sentences.zh: 所有的动物废料都倾倒进了河里。

sentences.en: And it was said that the river was so thick with filth
sentences.zh: 据说当时河里的污物浓稠到什么程度呢？

sentences.en: that a chicken could walk across it without getting her feet wet.
sentences.zh: 据说鸡走在上面都不会弄湿脚。

sentences.en: That's Elizabeth Colbert, author of the new book, Under a White Sky.
sentences.zh: 那是伊丽莎白·科尔伯特，新书《在白天下》的作者。

sentences.en: What needs to be also understood is that the Chicago River,
sentences.zh: 还需要了解的是，芝加哥河，

sentences.en: in its original incarnation, it flowed eastward into Lake Michigan,
sentences.zh: 在它最初的形态下，是向东流入密歇根湖的，

sentences.en: which was and still is Chicago's sole source of drinking water.
sentences.zh: 而密歇根湖过去是、现在依然是芝加哥唯一的饮用水源。

sentences.en: So to fix this problem, the city of Chicago carried out a massive project.
sentences.zh: 为了解决这个问题，芝加哥市实施了一项浩大的工程。

sentences.en: They reversed the river and sent the sewage water into the Mississippi.
sentences.zh: 他们逆转了河流，把污水排向了密西西比河。

sentences.en: When this enormous construction project was completed,
sentences.zh: 当这项巨大的工程完工时，

sentences.en: which was it was one of the most enormous construction projects of its era.
sentences.zh: 它确实是那个时代最宏大的建筑工程之一。

sentences.en: There was a facetious headline in the New York Times.
sentences.zh: 《纽约时报》当时还刊登了一个戏谑的标题。

sentences.en: It said something like water in the Chicago River resembles liquid again.
sentences.zh: 大意是说芝加哥河里的水看起来又像液体了。

sentences.en: By the way, if you want to know more about how it's even possible to reverse the river,
sentences.zh: 顺便说一下，如果你想了解逆转河流究竟是如何实现的，

sentences.en: we did a whole story about it.
sentences.zh: 我们专门做过一期节目。

sentences.en: Episode 86.
sentences.zh: 第86集。

sentences.en: It's a good one.
sentences.zh: 那集很不错。

sentences.en: Anyway, the river reversal was a big success.
sentences.zh: 总之，河流逆转工程取得了巨大成功。

sentences.en: Chicagoans had a reliable supply of clean drinking water.
sentences.zh: 芝加哥人从此有了可靠的清洁饮用水供应。

sentences.en: But like many large-scale human interventions, there were unintended consequences.
sentences.zh: 但就像许多大规模的人类干预一样，它也带来了意想不到的后果。

sentences.en: The reversal meant two unconnected drainage systems,
sentences.zh: 这次逆转意味着两个原本不相连的排水系统，

sentences.en: the Great Lakes and the Mississippi, were suddenly linked up,
sentences.zh: 即五大湖和密西西比河，突然被连接在了一起，

sentences.en: and that invasive species could move from one to the other.
sentences.zh: 而入侵物种可以从一个系统移动到另一个系统。

sentences.en: Both the Great Lakes and the Mississippi system became highly invaded water systems,
sentences.zh: 五大湖和密西西比河系统都成了深受入侵物种困扰的水系，

sentences.en: especially the Great Lakes.
sentences.zh: 尤其是五大湖。

sentences.en: The Great Lakes are like, there's like 180 known invasive species established in the Great Lakes.
sentences.zh: 五大湖的情况是，据了解，已有约180种入侵物种在五大湖安家落户。

sentences.en: And the species of interest right now, sort of as it was put to me by one engineer
sentences.zh: 而目前备受关注的物种，正如一位工程师，

sentences.en: or the Army Corps of Engineers, is Asian carp.
sentences.zh: 或者说美国陆军工程兵团的人对我所说的那样，是亚洲鲤鱼。

sentences.en: If Asian carp reached the Great Lakes, they could pretty much ruin everything.
sentences.zh: 如果亚洲鲤鱼进入五大湖，它们几乎会毁掉一切。

sentences.en: They would eat all of the endangered mollusks and even threaten the safety of human beings.
sentences.zh: 它们会吃光所有濒危软体动物，甚至威胁到人类的安全。

sentences.en: One of the species has the very annoying habit, from a human perspective,
sentences.zh: 其中一种鱼有一个从人类角度来看非常讨厌的习惯，

sentences.en: of flinging itself out of the water when it's disturbed.
sentences.zh: 那就是在受到惊扰时会从水里跃出。

sentences.en: And what disturbs it, often, is a boat, a motor, sound of a motor.
sentences.zh: 而惊扰它们的通常是船只、马达，或者马达的声音。

sentences.en: And so you get, you know, man v.
sentences.zh: 所以你会看到，你知道的，人与，

sentences.en: fish, you get a lot of injuries.
sentences.zh: 鱼的较量，你会受很多伤。

sentences.en: You know, I met people whose eye sockets had been broken by Asian carp.
sentences.zh: 我见过有人眼眶被亚洲鲤鱼撞碎了。

sentences.en: Faced with this epidemic of fish jumping out of the water and smacking people in the face,
sentences.zh: 面对这种鱼类跃出水面猛击人脸的流行病，

sentences.en: the Army Corps of Engineers were told, well, you have to fix this.
sentences.zh: 陆军工程兵团被告知，好吧，你们必须解决这个问题。

sentences.en: And they came up with a series of plans to stop the carp from migrating up the Chicago River.
sentences.zh: 于是他们提出了一系列计划来阻止鲤鱼沿芝加哥河上溯。

sentences.en: Like zapping the river with UV radiation, or putting in a big filtration system,
sentences.zh: 比如用紫外线照射河流，或者安装大型过滤系统，

sentences.en: or dumping nitrogen in the water to basically poison the fish.
sentences.zh: 或者往水里倾倒氮气来毒死这些鱼。

sentences.en: But what they eventually arrived at was the idea of setting up an electric barrier in the water.
sentences.zh: 但他们最终采取的方案是在水中设置一道电屏障。

sentences.en: This underwater sort of U-shaped, you know, structure that has these nodes in it
sentences.zh: 这是一种水下的U型结构，你知道的，上面装有节点，

sentences.en: that just pulses a lot of voltage through there.
sentences.zh: 通过这些节点向水中释放高压电流。

sentences.en: So just to recap, we dumped sewage into a river,
sentences.zh: 所以总结一下，我们先是往河里倾倒污水，

sentences.en: then reversed its flow by connecting it to an entirely different river,
sentences.zh: 然后通过连接另一条完全不同的河流来逆转它的流向，

sentences.en: and finally, we electrocuted the river.
sentences.zh: 最后，我们给这条河通了电。

sentences.en: This is something humans do a lot.
sentences.zh: 这是人类经常做的事情。

sentences.en: We meddle with nature.
sentences.zh: 我们干预自然。

sentences.en: And years later, we discover that that creates a whole bunch of unintended consequences.
sentences.zh: 多年后，我们发现这带来了一连串意想不到的后果。

sentences.en: And then, we have to meddle with nature all over again.
sentences.zh: 然后，我们又不得不再次干预自然。

sentences.en: These kinds of interventions are the subject of Elizabeth Colbert's new book.
sentences.zh: 这类干预措施正是伊丽莎白·科尔伯特新书的主题。

sentences.en: Today, we're going to talk with Colbert about all the extreme lengths humans will go
sentences.zh: 今天，我们将与科尔伯特探讨人类为了，

sentences.en: to try to undo our mistakes.
sentences.zh: 试图弥补错误而采取的各种极端手段。

sentences.en: There's so many examples of situations where people intervene
sentences.zh: 有太多的例子显示人们为了，

sentences.en: to undo the consequences of previous interventions.
sentences.zh: 弥补之前干预措施的后果而再次进行干预。

sentences.en: But one that really caught me in your book is the introduction of cane toads in Australia.
sentences.zh: 但书中有一个例子让我印象深刻，那就是在澳大利亚引入海蟾蜍。

sentences.en: So let's start right there.
sentences.zh: 那么我们就从这里开始吧。

sentences.en: Like, how did cane toads get to Australia?
sentences.zh: 海蟾蜍是怎么进入澳大利亚的？

sentences.en: So cane toads are native to South America and Central America
sentences.zh: 海蟾蜍原产于南美洲和中美洲，

sentences.en: and the very southernmost tip of Texas, actually.
sentences.zh: 实际上还有德克萨斯州的最南端。

sentences.en: They were introduced all around the world, interestingly enough,
sentences.zh: 有趣的是，它们被引入到了世界各地，

sentences.en: into the Caribbean, into Hawaii, and into Australia under the theory,
sentences.zh: 加勒比地区、夏威夷，还有澳大利亚，基于一种理论，

sentences.en: and I don't know where this theory came from,
sentences.zh: 我不知道这个理论是从哪来的，

sentences.en: that they were going to eat the beetles or the beetle grubs that plague sugarcane crops.
sentences.zh: 说是它们会吃掉危害甘蔗作物的甲虫或甲虫幼虫。

sentences.en: And so they were introduced into a lot of sugar-producing areas.
sentences.zh: 所以它们被引入到了许多产糖区。

sentences.en: And they were introduced into Australia in the 1930s
sentences.zh: 它们在20世纪30年代被引入澳大利亚，

sentences.en: in the hope that they were going to do something about these pests
sentences.zh: 希望能借此解决这些害虫问题，

sentences.en: in northeast Australia, which is a big sugarcane-growing region.
sentences.zh: 地点在澳大利亚东北部，那里是主要的甘蔗种植区。

sentences.en: Now, I think right now the consensus would be they did nothing.
sentences.zh: 现在，我想目前的共识是它们什么也没做。

sentences.en: They did absolutely nothing for the sugarcane.
sentences.zh: 它们对甘蔗完全没有起到任何作用。

sentences.en: But they were, like the Asian carp, highly successful invaders.
sentences.zh: 但它们就像亚洲鲤鱼一样，是极其成功的入侵者。

sentences.en: They have, you know, basically no natural predators.
sentences.zh: 它们基本上没有天敌，

sentences.en: They're highly toxic.
sentences.zh: 而且剧毒无比。

sentences.en: So anything that does try to eat them drops dead very quickly,
sentences.zh: 所以任何试图吃掉它们的动物都会很快毙命，

sentences.en: which has been a huge problem for Australia's native wildlife.
sentences.zh: 这对澳大利亚的本土野生动物来说是个巨大的问题。

sentences.en: But they continue to expand around Australia in a coastal region,
sentences.zh: 但它们继续在澳大利亚的沿海地区扩张，

sentences.en: sort of a ring around Australia.
sentences.zh: 就像在澳大利亚周围形成了一个环。

sentences.en: They can't survive very well in the center of Australia, which is simply too arid.
sentences.zh: 它们在澳大利亚中部很难生存，因为那里实在太干旱了。

sentences.en: But they're very good at exploiting any source of water.
sentences.zh: 但它们非常善于利用任何水源。

sentences.en: And I myself saw this when I went looking for them one night,
sentences.zh: 我有一天晚上出去寻找它们时亲眼见证了这一点，

sentences.en: and wherever there was a little puddle from an air conditioner or whatever,
sentences.zh: 无论哪里有空调滴水形成的小水洼，

sentences.en: there were cane toads.
sentences.zh: 那里就有海蟾蜍。

sentences.en: Mm-hmm.
sentences.zh: 嗯。

sentences.en: And they're particularly pernicious because they can eat anything.
sentences.zh: 它们特别有害，因为它们什么都吃。

sentences.en: So they're sort of detrimental to everything below them on the food chain.
sentences.zh: 所以它们对食物链中处于它们之下的所有生物都有害。

sentences.en: And they're so toxic, they're detrimental to all the predators
sentences.zh: 而且它们毒性太强，对所有捕食者也都有害，

sentences.en: because when a predator tries to eat them, they kill them.
sentences.zh: 因为当捕食者试图吃掉它们时，它们会把捕食者毒死。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: And another thing that is important to add here is that Australia has no native toads.
sentences.zh: 这里还有一点很重要，那就是澳大利亚没有本土蟾蜍。

sentences.en: So toads are just a whole, you know, class of organisms that did not get to Australia,
sentences.zh: 所以蟾蜍属于那种根本没能进入澳大利亚的生物类别，

sentences.en: I suppose Australia has been quite isolated for quite a long time, evolutionarily.
sentences.zh: 我想澳大利亚在进化史上已经孤立了很长一段时间了。

sentences.en: You know, there have been interventions, kind of, I don't know,
sentences.zh: 你知道，一直以来都有一些干预措施，怎么说呢，

sentences.en: more homegrown style interventions to deal with cane toads from the beginning.
sentences.zh: 更本土化的干预方式来对付海蟾蜍。

sentences.en: Can you talk about toad busters?
sentences.zh: 你能谈谈“捕蟾者”吗？

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 可以。

sentences.en: So toad killing in Australia is a major pastime.
sentences.zh: 在澳大利亚，捕杀蟾蜍是一项主要的消遣活动。

sentences.en: People bash toads with golf clubs.
sentences.zh: 人们用高尔夫球杆击打蟾蜍。

sentences.en: They run them over their lawnmowers.
sentences.zh: 用割草机碾压它们。

sentences.en: They organize, you know, toad-busting militias to go out and capture toads.
sentences.zh: 他们组织了“捕蟾民兵”出去捕捉蟾蜍。

sentences.en: And they put them in the freezer, which, you know, eventually kills them.
sentences.zh: 然后把它们放进冰箱，这样最终会杀死它们。

sentences.en: But supposedly painlessly, they've come up with sprays.
sentences.zh: 据说这样比较无痛，他们还发明了喷雾剂。

sentences.en: They are constantly looking for ways to reduce their numbers.
sentences.zh: 他们一直在寻找减少蟾蜍数量的方法。

sentences.en: But when you're talking about, I don't even know if there's an estimate of how many,
sentences.zh: 但当你谈论这个时，我甚至不知道有没有具体的数量估计，

sentences.en: hundreds of millions, it's pretty hard to make a dent in them.
sentences.zh: 数以亿计，想要减少它们的数量非常困难。

sentences.en: As cane toads make their way across the Australian coast,
sentences.zh: 随着海蟾蜍在澳大利亚海岸蔓延，

sentences.en: the government is considering more high-tech interventions to stop them.
sentences.zh: 政府正在考虑采取更高端的技术干预手段来阻止它们。

sentences.en: One of those measures is using CRISPR,
sentences.zh: 其中一项措施是使用CRISPR，

sentences.en: which is a technique that allows scientists to make small tweaks to DNA.
sentences.zh: 这是一种允许科学家对DNA进行微调的技术。

sentences.en: This particular project that I visited at this highly biosecure facility outside of Melbourne,
sentences.zh: 我参观了墨尔本郊外一个高度生物安全的设施，这个特定的项目，

sentences.en: they were using CRISPR to produce toads that were less toxic.
sentences.zh: 他们正在利用CRISPR培育毒性较低的海蟾蜍。

sentences.en: They had disabled the gene that creates an enzyme that makes this toxin so potent.
sentences.zh: 他们禁用了产生某种酶的基因，而这种酶正是导致毒素如此强效的原因。

sentences.en: There are two good reasons to make cane toads less toxic.
sentences.zh: 培育毒性较低的海蟾蜍有两个好处。

sentences.en: For one thing, they won't kill their predators when they're eaten.
sentences.zh: 首先，它们被吃掉时不会毒死捕食者。

sentences.en: But also, the predators learn a valuable lesson,
sentences.zh: 其次，捕食者会吸取一个宝贵的教训，

sentences.en: that cane toads taste bad and will make you sick.
sentences.zh: 那就是海蟾蜍味道很差，吃了会生病。

sentences.en: This has a lot of potential to mitigate the bad effects of cane toads.
sentences.zh: 这在减轻海蟾蜍负面影响方面有很大的潜力。

sentences.en: But for many people, it's a bridge too far.
sentences.zh: 但对许多人来说，这太过火了。

sentences.en: You could potentially disrupt reproduction.
sentences.zh: 你可能会破坏它们的繁殖能力。

sentences.en: So you could potentially have cane toads out there that could not reproduce.
sentences.zh: 所以你可能会培育出无法繁殖的海蟾蜍。

sentences.en: And if you manage to spread that trait,
sentences.zh: 如果你能设法传播这种特性，

sentences.en: then you could potentially make a big dent in the cane toad population.
sentences.zh: 那么你就有可能大幅减少海蟾蜍的数量。

sentences.en: But there's a lot of steps along the way.
sentences.zh: 但这一过程中还有很多步骤。

sentences.en: And evolution being what it is,
sentences.zh: 而且进化就是这样，

sentences.en: the question of whether you could do that is unclear.
sentences.zh: 你是否真的能做到这一点还不清楚。

sentences.en: So the difference between toad busting or even electrifying carp in a river
sentences.zh: 所以，捕杀蟾蜍甚至给河里的鲤鱼通电，

sentences.en: and using CRISPR, it feels different.
sentences.zh: 与使用CRISPR之间的区别，感觉是不一样的。

sentences.en: It might not be different.
sentences.zh: 也许并没有什么不同。

sentences.en: How does it feel to you?
sentences.zh: 你感觉如何？

sentences.en: Do those things feel different to you?
sentences.zh: 你觉得这些事情有什么不同吗？

sentences.en: Well, I think that there's sort of this interesting continuum
sentences.zh: 嗯，我认为这存在一种有趣的连续性，

sentences.en: and somewhat slippery slope.
sentences.zh: 而且在某种程度上是一条滑坡谬误。

sentences.en: And I think that people will, you know, look at one intervention and say,
sentences.zh: 我认为人们会看着某项干预措施说，

sentences.en: oh, yeah, you know, that made sense.
sentences.zh: 哦，是的，那是有道理的。

sentences.en: And the next one, oh, that made sense.
sentences.zh: 然后下一个，哦，那也有道理。

sentences.en: You know, and then you kind of go along and go,
sentences.zh: 你知道，然后你继续走下去，会说，

sentences.en: hmm, maybe I'm not so cool about that with that.
sentences.zh: 嗯，对于那个，我可能不太能接受。

sentences.en: You know, but I don't subscribe to the notion
sentences.zh: 你知道，但我并不认同那种观点，

sentences.en: that there's clearly interventions on one side
sentences.zh: 即一边是明确的干预，

sentences.en: and clearly interventions on another.
sentences.zh: 另一边也是明确的干预。

sentences.en: They're gray scale, I guess, basically.
sentences.zh: 我想它们基本上是灰色的渐变。

sentences.en: And where one draws the line is a very individual choice.
sentences.zh: 至于在哪里划定界限，是一个非常个人的选择。

sentences.en: But I think one of the points of the book is also to try to challenge a little bit,
sentences.zh: 但我认为这本书的目的之一也是试图挑战一下，

sentences.en: or maybe more than a little bit, you know, where people do draw the line.
sentences.zh: 或者说甚至不止一点点，你知道，人们总会划定界限。

sentences.en: Because gene editing is a technique, for example,
sentences.zh: 因为基因编辑是一项技术，举个例子，

sentences.en: that a lot of people find anathema, you know, and just shouldn't do it.
sentences.zh: 很多人觉得这是禁忌，你知道，觉得根本不该做。

sentences.en: Now, to be frank, we already do do it a lot, a lot, a lot.
sentences.zh: 但坦白说，我们其实已经在做了，而且做了很多很多。

sentences.en: Every, I guarantee you, you know, you ate some genetically modified organism
sentences.zh: 我敢保证，你知道，你过去几天里肯定吃过某种转基因生物，

sentences.en: in the last few days, you know.
sentences.zh: 你知道的。

sentences.en: It's gene edited corn, gene edited soy is ubiquitous in the US.
sentences.zh: 在美国，基因编辑玉米和基因编辑大豆随处可见。

sentences.en: But still people might say, well, you know, I don't want to,
sentences.zh: 但人们可能还是会说，嗯，你知道，我不想要，

sentences.en: I don't want anything out on the landscape.
sentences.zh: 我不希望任何东西出现在自然环境中。

sentences.en: Certain organisms may not be on the landscape.
sentences.zh: 有些生物可能确实不该出现在自然环境中。

sentences.en: And I use the example of the American chestnut,
sentences.zh: 我举过美国栗树的例子，

sentences.en: which was devastated, destroyed, basically,
sentences.zh: 它基本上被栗疫病摧毁了，灭绝了，

sentences.en: driven to the very edge of extinction by chestnut blight.
sentences.zh: 被逼到了灭绝的边缘。

sentences.en: Now, scientists in Syracuse, New York,
sentences.zh: 现在，纽约州雪城大学的科学家们，

sentences.en: have developed a blight-resistant chestnut that's a transgenic tree.
sentences.zh: 研发出了一种抗疫病的栗树，那是一种转基因树。

sentences.en: And, you know, the choice is sort of between this tree
sentences.zh: 你知道，选择其实就在这棵树之间，

sentences.en: that has one little gene tweaked that allows it to be resistant to chestnut blight
sentences.zh: 它只微调了一个基因，就能抵御栗疫病，

sentences.en: or no chestnuts.
sentences.zh: 或者选择根本没有栗树。

sentences.en: And that's a tough choice in my view.
sentences.zh: 在我看来，这是一个艰难的选择。

sentences.en: We've been genetically modifying plants for 10,000 years.
sentences.zh: 我们进行植物基因改造已经有一万年了。

sentences.en: I mean, look, you've probably eaten transgenic corn,
sentences.zh: 我是说，你看，你可能吃过转基因玉米，

sentences.en: but you've also eaten regular corn, which is the result of agriculture,
sentences.zh: 但你也吃过普通玉米，那是农业的产物，

sentences.en: which is maybe the biggest human intervention that there is.
sentences.zh: 这或许是人类有史以来最大的干预行为。

sentences.en: This line between what is a natural intervention
sentences.zh: 这种所谓的自然干预

sentences.en: versus what is an unnatural intervention is really curious to me.
sentences.zh: 与非自然干预之间的界限，让我感到非常好奇。

sentences.en: What do you think about that?
sentences.zh: 你是怎么看的？

sentences.en: Yeah, I mean, I think you're right.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我是说，我觉得你说得对。

sentences.en: It gets very much to this point that there's a continuum, right?
sentences.zh: 这确实触及到了一个连续谱的问题，对吧？

sentences.en: I don't think there are too many people around in 2021 who say,
sentences.zh: 我不认为2021年还有多少人会说，

sentences.en: you know, plant breeding, that really shouldn't be screwing around with that.
sentences.zh: 你知道，植物育种，真的不该去瞎搞那个。

sentences.en: You know, that's just too, that's just a, you know, bridge too far.
sentences.zh: 你知道，那太过了，那简直是，你知道，越界了。

sentences.en: You know, it gets to that idea that what you're used to, you're used to,
sentences.zh: 你知道，这归结于一种习惯，你习惯了什么就是什么，

sentences.en: you know, you're used to acres and acres and acres
sentences.zh: 你知道，你习惯了那一亩又一亩，

sentences.en: and a whole state's worth of corn.
sentences.zh: 甚至整个州都是玉米。

sentences.en: And as you say, corn itself is a product of, you know,
sentences.zh: 正如你所说，玉米本身就是，你知道，

sentences.en: many, many hundreds or thousands of years of very careful breeding.
sentences.zh: 几百甚至几千年来精心培育的产物。

sentences.en: But, you know, well, it's there.
sentences.zh: 但是，你知道，嗯，它就在那儿。

sentences.en: It's always been there.
sentences.zh: 它一直都在那儿。

sentences.en: Okay, I'm not appalled by that.
sentences.zh: 好吧，我对此并不感到震惊。

sentences.en: Then some people are, you know, appalled by GMO corn.
sentences.zh: 但有些人，你知道，对转基因玉米感到震惊。

sentences.en: Although, as I say, it's almost impossible to avoid in an American diet.
sentences.zh: 尽管正如我所说，在美国人的饮食中，这几乎是无法避免的。

sentences.en: That my goal is not to convince anyone not to be appalled.
sentences.zh: 我的目的不是说服任何人不要感到震惊。

sentences.en: But my goal is to challenge, you know, why are we appalled?
sentences.zh: 但我的目的是质疑，你知道，我们为什么会感到震惊？

sentences.en: Is it simply, you know, what we're used to?
sentences.zh: 仅仅是因为，你知道，我们习惯了什么吗？

sentences.en: You know, there are big trade-offs that are being made,
sentences.zh: 你知道，这里面存在巨大的权衡，

sentences.en: to a large extent, unwittingly.
sentences.zh: 在很大程度上，人们是在不知不觉中做出的。

sentences.en: And when you bring them to the level of consciousness,
sentences.zh: 而当你把这些问题提升到意识层面时，

sentences.en: the questions become pretty complicated.
sentences.zh: 问题就变得相当复杂了。

sentences.en: As we go up the scale of human interventions,
sentences.zh: 随着我们人类干预规模的扩大，

sentences.en: since climate change is pretty much the biggest way
sentences.zh: 因为气候变化几乎是人类

sentences.en: people have messed with nature.
sentences.zh: 干扰自然最大的方式。

sentences.en: And it's becoming clear that just reducing our CO2 emissions
sentences.zh: 而且越来越清楚的是，仅仅减少二氧化碳排放

sentences.en: won't be enough to stop global warming,
sentences.zh: 不足以阻止全球变暖，

sentences.en: even if we get to net zero.
sentences.zh: 即使我们实现了净零排放。

sentences.en: So scientists are talking about a series of interventions
sentences.zh: 所以科学家们正在讨论一系列干预措施，

sentences.en: called geoengineering.
sentences.zh: 称为地球工程。

sentences.en: And they are pretty controversial,
sentences.zh: 它们非常有争议，

sentences.en: since they involve messing with the chemistry of the atmosphere.
sentences.zh: 因为它们涉及干扰大气化学。

sentences.en: One of these technologies is called carbon capture and storage.
sentences.zh: 其中一项技术被称为碳捕集与封存。

sentences.en: I mean, when you hear all this talk now of going net zero,
sentences.zh: 我是说，当你现在听到所有关于实现净零排放的讨论时，

sentences.en: in carbon emissions, what's the net?
sentences.zh: 碳排放的“净”是指什么？

sentences.en: Well, the net is, you know, you're still going to have
sentences.zh: 嗯，净值就是，你知道，你仍然会有

sentences.en: a certain amount of emissions,
sentences.zh: 一定量的排放，

sentences.en: and you're going to have to counter that,
sentences.zh: 而你必须抵消它，

sentences.en: balance that with negative emissions.
sentences.zh: 用负排放来平衡它。

sentences.en: So negative emissions are just sucking CO2 out of the atmosphere somehow.
sentences.zh: 所以负排放就是以某种方式从大气中吸收二氧化碳。

sentences.en: We can talk about how, if you'd like.
sentences.zh: 如果你愿意，我们可以谈谈具体怎么做。

sentences.en: And storing it somehow.
sentences.zh: 并以某种方式储存起来。

sentences.en: You actually spent a lot of money on a carbon capture system
sentences.zh: 你实际上花了很多钱在一个碳捕集系统上，

sentences.en: where you paid a company to offset your emissions in Europe.
sentences.zh: 你付钱给一家公司来抵消你在欧洲的排放。

sentences.en: What happened there?
sentences.zh: 那件事怎么样了？

sentences.en: So I, yes, I still spend money.
sentences.zh: 所以我，是的，我还在花钱。

sentences.en: I pay a Swiss-based company every month a sum of money.
sentences.zh: 我每个月付给一家瑞士公司一笔钱。

sentences.en: And the idea is that they, actually, this machinery is in Iceland.
sentences.zh: 他们的想法是，实际上，这套机器在冰岛。

sentences.en: They suck some CO2 emissions out of the air.
sentences.zh: 他们从空气中吸收了一些二氧化碳排放。

sentences.en: They're, you know, attributed to me.
sentences.zh: 它们，你知道，归功于我。

sentences.en: They suck out some CO2.
sentences.zh: 他们吸收了一些二氧化碳。

sentences.en: Unfortunately, it's only a small fraction of my actual emissions.
sentences.zh: 不幸的是，这只是我实际排放量的一小部分。

sentences.en: And they do that in this machine that looks like kind of a giant air conditioner.
sentences.zh: 他们用一台看起来像巨型空调的机器来做这件事。

sentences.en: Then they pipe the CO2 very deep underground in Iceland where all the rock is volcanic rock.
sentences.zh: 然后他们把二氧化碳输送到冰岛地底深处，那里全是火山岩。

sentences.en: And, you know, under heat and pressure and with a lot of water, actually,
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道，在高温高压和大量水的作用下，实际上，

sentences.en: there's a chemical reaction where the CO2 reacts with the rock and forms calcium carbonate.
sentences.zh: 发生了一种化学反应，二氧化碳与岩石反应生成了碳酸钙。

sentences.en: So it's, you know, locked up there underground, presumably permanently.
sentences.zh: 所以它，你知道，被锁在那里，大概是永久性的。

sentences.en: So that is one form of carbon dioxide removal.
sentences.zh: 所以这是一种二氧化碳清除形式。

sentences.en: And so what are the pros and cons of this?
sentences.zh: 那么这有什么利弊呢？

sentences.en: I mean, does it really solve the problem?
sentences.zh: 我是说，它真的能解决问题吗？

sentences.en: What do you think of it?
sentences.zh: 你怎么看？

sentences.en: Well, the pros is you're taking, you know, you're taking CO2 out of the air and you're locking it up.
sentences.zh: 嗯，好处是你正在，你知道，你正在从空气中吸收二氧化碳并将其锁住。

sentences.en: So that is the obvious pro.
sentences.zh: 所以这是显而易见的好处。

sentences.en: The cons are the question of practicality at scale.
sentences.zh: 坏处是规模化应用的可行性问题。

sentences.en: How's that?
sentences.zh: 怎么说？

sentences.en: I mean, the whole project that I visited in Iceland and they're scaling it up.
sentences.zh: 我是说，我在冰岛参观的整个项目，他们正在扩大规模。

sentences.en: It's supposed to be able to deal with 4,000 tons of CO2 a year, okay, which, you know,
sentences.zh: 它应该能够每年处理4000吨二氧化碳，好吧，这，你知道，

sentences.en: might sound like a lot, but is ridiculously trivial compared to the 40 billion tons of CO2
sentences.zh: 听起来可能很多，但与人类每年通过燃烧化石燃料

sentences.en: that humans pour into the atmosphere by burning fossil fuels every year.
sentences.zh: 排入大气的400亿吨二氧化碳相比，简直微不足道。

sentences.en: So when you think about that, and it takes energy to get my CO2 out of the atmosphere in Iceland,
sentences.zh: 所以当你想到这一点时，而且在冰岛从大气中提取我的二氧化碳需要能量，

sentences.en: you know, one of the reasons this project is located in Iceland for all sorts of reasons,
sentences.zh: 你知道，这个项目位于冰岛的原因之一，出于各种原因，

sentences.en: it's located actually at a geothermal plant, which is making, you know, producing electricity
sentences.zh: 它实际上位于一个地热发电厂，它正在，你知道，利用地热能发电，

sentences.en: using the geothermal energy, you know, from the center of the earth.
sentences.zh: 你知道，来自地球中心的地热能。

sentences.en: But if you imagine doing this at huge scale, how are you getting that energy?
sentences.zh: 但如果你想象大规模这样做，你从哪里获得能量？

sentences.en: And then where are you putting this stuff?
sentences.zh: 然后你把这些东西放在哪里？

sentences.en: You know, there's room in basalt of Iceland for a lot of CO2, but, you know, not for all
sentences.zh: 你知道，冰岛的玄武岩里有容纳大量二氧化碳的空间，但是，你知道，装不下

sentences.en: of our CO2.
sentences.zh: 我们所有的二氧化碳。

sentences.en: So you have to locate these facilities in various places.
sentences.zh: 所以你必须在不同的地方建立这些设施。

sentences.en: You'd have to potentially start piping the CO2 around.
sentences.zh: 你可能需要开始到处铺设管道输送二氧化碳。

sentences.en: I mean, carbon dioxide removal using, you know, technology has to be, when you think about
sentences.zh: 我是说，利用技术进行二氧化碳清除，当你想到它时，

sentences.en: it, to make a difference on the scale of the energy infrastructure we have now.
sentences.zh: 必须要在我们现有的能源基础设施规模上产生影响。

sentences.en: And that's just huge.
sentences.zh: 而那规模太大了。

sentences.en: I don't know if you want to call them downsides, but those are the obvious, very evident obstacles.
sentences.zh: 我不知道你是否想称它们为缺点，但这些是显而易见、非常明显的障碍。

sentences.en: Another large-scale intervention like this that you wrote about is solar geoengineering.
sentences.zh: 你写过的另一种类似的大规模干预措施是太阳能地球工程。

sentences.en: And that's interventions that basically reflect the sun's rays back into space that would,
sentences.zh: 那是基本上将太阳光反射回太空的干预措施，理论上，

sentences.en: in theory, cool the temperature of the earth.
sentences.zh: 会冷却地球的温度。

sentences.en: And the idea is that we slow down global warming this way.
sentences.zh: 其理念是我们通过这种方式减缓全球变暖。

sentences.en: Obviously, it's experimental, it's untested.
sentences.zh: 显然，这是实验性的，未经测试。

sentences.en: How would it work?
sentences.zh: 它将如何运作？

sentences.en: There are all sorts of intermediate technologies here, too.
sentences.zh: 这里也有各种各样的中间技术。

sentences.en: So there's a technology referred to sometimes as marine cloud brightening, where we would
sentences.zh: 有一种有时被称为海洋云增亮的技术，我们会

sentences.en: manipulate clouds to make them whiter so they'd reflect more sunlight back to space.
sentences.zh: 操纵云层使其变白，从而将更多的阳光反射回太空。

sentences.en: That, in theory, is possible and, in theory, could have a sort of regional cooling effect.
sentences.zh: 理论上这是可能的，理论上可以产生某种区域性的冷却效果。

sentences.en: But the biggie, the big one that the book sort of builds to is this idea that you could spray
sentences.zh: 但最重大的，这本书所铺垫的重点是这个想法：你可以喷洒

sentences.en: some kind of reflective substance, particles, into the stratosphere.
sentences.zh: 某种反射物质，即颗粒，进入平流层。

sentences.en: These would bounce sunlight back to space before it hit the earth, so you'd really be getting
sentences.zh: 这些颗粒会在阳光到达地球之前将其弹回太空，所以你确实会得到

sentences.en: less direct sunlight on planet earth.
sentences.zh: 更少的直接阳光照射到地球上。

sentences.en: And that would have a cooling effect.
sentences.zh: 那会产生冷却效果。

sentences.en: Obviously, we haven't tried this on a large scale as humans, but there is a natural analog
sentences.zh: 显然，我们人类还没有在大规模上尝试过这个，但有一个自然的类比

sentences.en: to this with volcanoes spilling ash into the atmosphere.
sentences.zh: 就是火山将灰烬喷入大气层。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Well, it's not actually the ash that has this impact.
sentences.zh: 嗯，实际上产生这种影响的并不是灰烬。

sentences.en: In fact, it's the sulfur dioxide from volcanoes that gets, you know, ejected up into the stratosphere,
sentences.zh: 事实上，是火山喷出的二氧化硫被喷射到平流层中，

sentences.en: floats around, forms these tiny little, what are called aerosols, they're essentially little
sentences.zh: 四处漂浮，形成这些微小的颗粒，被称为气溶胶，它们本质上是小水滴，

sentences.en: droplets that are highly reflective, why you get such beautiful sunsets after a big eruption.
sentences.zh: 具有高度反射性，这就是为什么大喷发后会有如此美丽的日落。

sentences.en: And, you know, people have measured, after Mount Pinatubo in the 90s, climate scientists were
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道，人们测量过，90年代皮纳图博火山爆发后，气候科学家们

sentences.en: very interested in this effect, what effect would this have?
sentences.zh: 对这种效应非常感兴趣，这会有什么影响？

sentences.en: And they measured it pretty precisely, and it definitely led to a temporary drop in average
sentences.zh: 他们测量得相当精确，它确实导致了平均气温的暂时下降，

sentences.en: global temperatures as a result of this effect.
sentences.zh: 这是这种效应的结果。

sentences.en: And, you know, this has been understood for, you know, quite a while that volcanoes have this
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道，人们早就明白火山有这种

sentences.en: impact.
sentences.zh: 影响。

sentences.en: And so the idea behind solar geoengineering is, could we mimic that?
sentences.zh: 所以太阳能地球工程背后的想法是，我们能模仿它吗？

sentences.en: And people are also exploring different materials.
sentences.zh: 人们也在探索不同的材料。

sentences.en: People have even floated the idea of using diamond dust, you know, there are all sorts
sentences.zh: 人们甚至提出了使用钻石粉的想法，你知道，有各种各样的

sentences.en: of ideas out there.
sentences.zh: 想法。

sentences.en: For a long time, environmentalists have seen geoengineering as a total non-starter, because
sentences.zh: 长期以来，环保主义者一直认为地球工程完全不可行，因为

sentences.en: the argument is, it's a long shot if it would work at all, and it's a distraction from the
sentences.zh: 他们的论点是，它是否有效还很难说，而且它会分散人们对

sentences.en: real work of reducing carbon emissions.
sentences.zh: 减少碳排放这一真正工作的注意力。

sentences.en: What do you think of that criticism?
sentences.zh: 你怎么看这种批评？

sentences.en: Well, that, you know, that's a big concern.
sentences.zh: 嗯，那，你知道，那是一个很大的担忧。

sentences.en: This question of, if you dangle in front of people some way that we might be able to counteract
sentences.zh: 这个问题是，如果你在人们面前晃动某种可能抵消

sentences.en: climate change without actually reducing our emissions, you know, are you just going to
sentences.zh: 气候变化的方法，而不需要真正减少我们的排放，你知道，你是不是会

sentences.en: encourage people to, you know, behave badly?
sentences.zh: 鼓励人们，你知道，表现得更糟糕？

sentences.en: And I think that's a big worry.
sentences.zh: 我认为这是一个很大的担忧。

sentences.en: And I think it's a legitimate worry.
sentences.zh: 我认为这确实是一个合理的担忧。

sentences.en: On the other hand, we are behaving badly.
sentences.zh: 另一方面，我们的行为也很糟糕。

sentences.en: And so the counterargument is, even at the point that we do stop emitting CO2, we haven't
sentences.zh: 所以反方观点是，即使在我们停止排放二氧化碳的那一刻，我们也没有

sentences.en: gotten back the climate of the paSt.
sentences.zh: 回到过去的气候状态。

sentences.en: We've simply stopped putting more heating into the system.
sentences.zh: 我们只是停止了向系统中增加热量。

sentences.en: It'll take, you know, probably a few to several decades on some level, century scale to really,
sentences.zh: 这可能需要几十年甚至更久，在某种程度上，需要以世纪为单位，才能真正

sentences.en: you know, reach a new equilibrium.
sentences.zh: 达到一个新的平衡。

sentences.en: But, you know, you're going to continue to melt the ice caps.
sentences.zh: 但是，冰盖会继续融化。

sentences.en: You're going to continue to see sea level rise.
sentences.zh: 海平面会继续上升。

sentences.en: The oceans are going to continue to warm.
sentences.zh: 海洋会继续变暖。

sentences.en: So the counterargument is, well, you may find yourself in such a terrible situation that
sentences.zh: 所以反方观点是，好吧，你可能会发现自己处于如此糟糕的境地，以至于

sentences.en: you're going to want some way of counteracting some of that warming because the alternatives
sentences.zh: 你会想要某种方法来抵消部分变暖，因为其他选择

sentences.en: are so awful.
sentences.zh: 实在是太可怕了。

sentences.en: And I think that both of those are very legitimate arguments.
sentences.zh: 我认为这两种观点都非常合理。

sentences.en: The other part of this that's interesting is the word geo.
sentences.zh: 这件事另一个有趣的部分是“地球工程”（geoengineering）这个词。

sentences.en: I mean, it is a global thing.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这是一件全球性的事情。

sentences.en: And when you're talking about cane toads in Australia, it's at least limited to Australia.
sentences.zh: 当你谈论澳大利亚的海蟾蜍时，它至少局限于澳大利亚。

sentences.en: Who gets to decide who pours stuff into the stratosphere?
sentences.zh: 谁有权决定谁能向平流层倾倒物质？

sentences.en: It's very difficult to think through because, you know, we're not very good at global governments,
sentences.zh: 这很难思考，因为我们并不擅长全球治理，

sentences.en: you know, witness what's happened with climate change.
sentences.zh: 看看气候变化发生的事情就知道了。

sentences.en: And people have pointed out that a potentially frightening thing about geoengineering is it could be done, you know, in theory by one country or even, once again,
sentences.zh: 人们指出，地球工程一个潜在的可怕之处在于，理论上它可能由一个国家完成，甚至再次强调，

sentences.en: in theory by one very, very rich person.
sentences.zh: 理论上由一个非常有钱的人完成。

sentences.en: I don't, you know, personally, once again, this is, you know, one woman's opinion.
sentences.zh: 我个人并不觉得这是一个非常有说服力的论点，因为这不是你可以秘密进行的事情。

sentences.en: I don't find that a very compelling argument because this is not something you do in secret.
sentences.zh: 这需要你在平流层进行大量的飞行。

sentences.en: This is something that you are flying lots and lots of flights in the stratosphere.
sentences.zh: 如果我们不希望飞机出现在那里，我们当然知道如何从平流层击落它们。

sentences.en: We certainly know how to shoot down planes from the stratosphere if we don't want them there.
sentences.zh: 所以我认为，一群强大的国家可以集体做到这一点。

sentences.en: And so, you know, I think that a bunch of very powerful nations could do it, you know, collectively.
sentences.zh: 但我认为没有哪个国家能够独自行动。

sentences.en: But I don't think one country is going to be able to sort of go rogue here.
sentences.zh: 但关于如何决定以及谁有权决定，我没有好的答案。

sentences.en: But the question of how you decide and who gets to decide, I don't have a good answer for that.
sentences.zh: 我认为没有人有好的答案。

sentences.en: I don't think anyone has a good answer for that.
sentences.zh: 显而易见的机构，我想应该是联合国。

sentences.en: You know, the obvious body, I guess, would be the UN.
sentences.zh: 但是，自联合国成立以来，我们在某种程度上真正达成过什么共识吗？

sentences.en: But, you know, what have we really been able to agree on as a world since the UN was founded on some level?
sentences.zh: 关键是，联合国的权力大小取决于我们赋予它多少权力。

sentences.en: The UN is only as powerful as we say it is, is the thing, yeah.
sentences.zh: 所以，有很多风险和理由不去进行这类事情。

sentences.en: So there are a lot of risks and reasons to not do this kind of thing.
sentences.zh: 但有一种观点认为，为了减轻气候变化的影响，我们需要某种形式的地球工程，因为我们已经排放了太多的碳。

sentences.en: But there's an argument that to mitigate the impact of climate change, we need some form of geoengineering because we've already just emitted so much carbon.
sentences.zh: 你在写这本书的时候，对地球工程的看法有改变吗？

sentences.en: Did your opinion on geoengineering change at all when you were writing this book?
sentences.zh: 我当然认为这本书表达了对我们竟然会考虑这件事的极大忧虑。

sentences.en: I certainly think that the book expresses a lot of trepidation about even, you know, that we'd even be considering this.
sentences.zh: 我在一次采访中将其描述为一种“敬畏的恐惧”。

sentences.en: I think I described it in one interview as a sort of respectful horror.
sentences.zh: 但我确实发现，那些从事这项工作的科学家们的论点非常聪明，他们比我更深入地了解

sentences.en: But I do, I did find the arguments of people working on it who were very, very smart scientists, you know, really, really smart and a lot more immersed in, you know,
sentences.zh: 大气科学。

sentences.en: the science of the atmosphere than I am, certainly.
sentences.zh: 他们的观点是，看，现在有很多关于修复气候或扭转气候变化的讨论。

sentences.en: The argument that, look, there's a lot of talk now about fixing the climate or reversing climate change.
sentences.zh: 那是不可能的。

sentences.en: That's not possible.
sentences.zh: 这里唯一的可能性是二氧化碳清除。

sentences.en: The only possibility here is, you know, carbon dioxide removal.
sentences.zh: 但这仍然非常缓慢。

sentences.en: That's still very slow.
sentences.zh: 这不会很快产生影响。

sentences.en: That's not going to have an impact faSt.
sentences.zh: 我们没有太多应对气候变化的快速手段。

sentences.en: We don't have a lot of, you know, weapons in our quiver for doing anything about climate change faSt.
sentences.zh: 我发现那次谈话比我预想的要更令人不安。

sentences.en: I found that conversation to be more fraught, I suppose, than I expected going in.
sentences.zh: 这并不意味着我完全改变了看法，但我必须说，确实可以提出一些令人信服的论点。

sentences.en: That doesn't mean that I exactly changed my view on it, but I have to say that some compelling arguments can be made.
sentences.zh: 休息之后，继续与伊丽莎白·科尔伯特（Elizabeth Kolbert）对话。

sentences.en: After the break, more with Elizabeth Kolber.
sentences.zh: 当你想到我们的干预和反干预时，很容易将所有这些干预视为彻底的灾难。

sentences.en: When you think about our interventions and the counter-interventions, it's pretty easy to consider all of those interventions as unmitigated disasters.
sentences.zh: 但这是一种选择性偏差，因为有很多人们非常喜欢的干预措施，比如养狗。

sentences.en: But it's kind of a selection bias because there are lots of interventions that people like an awful lot, like doggies, for example.
sentences.zh: 因为狗的存在仅仅是因为人类干预并驯化了狼。

sentences.en: Because dogs only exist because humans intervened and domesticated wolves.
sentences.zh: 绝对是这样。

sentences.en: Absolutely.
sentences.zh: 我把你的观点原封不动地告诉了大卫·基思（David Keith），他是主要的科学家之一，

sentences.en: And I put that exactly what you're saying to David Keith, who's really one of the chief scientists,
sentences.zh: 可能比地球上任何人都花更多时间思考地球工程，他是哈佛大学的应用物理学教授。

sentences.en: probably spent more time thinking about geoengineering than anyone else on Earth, a professor of, I think, applied physics at Harvard.
sentences.zh: 他说，是的，你表现出了你的偏见，不可能计算出我们认为这些干预措施中有多少是好是坏，

sentences.en: And he said, yes, you're showing your biases, you know, it's impossible to do that calculation of how many of these interventions, you know, we would consider good or bad,
sentences.zh: 从农业开始，正如你所说，驯化玉米、小麦和水稻。

sentences.en: you know, starting with agriculture, as you say, you know, domesticating corn and wheat and rice.
sentences.zh: 那是一个糟糕的选择吗？

sentences.en: Was that a bad choice?
sentences.zh: 有些人会说是的，贾雷德·戴蒙德（Jared Diamond）称农业是人类历史上最糟糕的错误。

sentences.en: Some people would say, yes, Jared Diamond has called agriculture, you know, the worst mistake in human history.
sentences.zh: 但我们已经走到这一步了，没有回头路了。

sentences.en: But here we are, and there's no going back from that.
sentences.zh: 我们不会放弃农业。

sentences.en: We're not getting rid of agriculture.
sentences.zh: 那是肯定的。

sentences.en: That's for damn sure.
sentences.zh: 我们可以对过去一万年或更长时间里做出的许多选择感到后悔。

sentences.en: We can regret a lot of choices that have been made over the last 10,000 years or longer even.
sentences.zh: 但现在地球上有近80亿人口，我们无法回头。

sentences.en: But we can't turn around now with, you know, almost 8 billion people on the planet.
sentences.zh: 那根本不是一个选择。

sentences.en: That's just not really an option.
sentences.zh: 关于心理学，我发现特别迷人的一点是当你谈到新奥尔良时。

sentences.en: Something about the psychology that I found really fascinating is particularly when you were talking about New Orleans.
sentences.zh: 新奥尔良这个地方，从水文学的角度来看，根本就不应该存在。

sentences.en: So, you know, New Orleans is a place that, by all accounts, at least in terms of hydrology, shouldn't exiSt.
sentences.zh: 它从一开始就是一场斗争。

sentences.en: It was a struggle from the beginning.
sentences.zh: 它依然是一场斗争，既要保持干燥以供居住，又要保持足够湿润以作为港口，这对我来说是新信息。

sentences.en: It remains a struggle, both to keep it dry enough to live on and, surprisingly, keeping it wet enough to be a port, which was new information to me.
sentences.zh: 但很明显，我们将永远不断地进行干预，以维持新奥尔良的运转。

sentences.en: But it's clear that we will always pile intervention upon intervention to keep New Orleans going.
sentences.zh: 这就是我们吗？

sentences.en: Is this just who we are?
sentences.zh: 我认为新奥尔良是这种现象的一个很好的例子。

sentences.en: Well, I think that New Orleans is a great example of this phenomenon.
sentences.zh: 它位于密西西比河汇入墨西哥湾的绝佳位置。

sentences.en: It's, you know, at a perfect location where the Mississippi hits the Gulf.
sentences.zh: 1718年法国人战略性地决定在此定居时，它还是一片沼泽。

sentences.en: It was a swamp when the French strategically decided to settle it in 1718.
sentences.zh: 在此之前，人们也曾居住在该地区。

sentences.en: And, you know, prior to that, people had lived in the area.
sentences.zh: 美洲原住民在密西西比三角洲生活了数千年。

sentences.en: Native Americans had been living in the Mississippi Delta for, you know, thousands of years.
sentences.zh: 但他们并没有坚持住在洪水季节会被淹没的地方。

sentences.en: But they didn't insist on staying in a place that was going to get flooded during flood season.
sentences.zh: 一旦你开始成为一个定居的物种，建造城市并拥有巨大的基础设施，你就投入了这些基础设施。

sentences.en: Once you start being a sedentary, you know, species that builds cities and has tremendous infrastructure, you're invested in that infrastructure.
sentences.zh: 新奥尔良现在正在发生这种情况，越来越多的巨大干预措施。

sentences.en: And that was happening in New Orleans right now, more and more humongous interventions.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，即使是卡特里娜飓风之后建造的东西，也只是大规模的水利工程。

sentences.en: I mean, just, you know, even just what was built after Katrina, just massive, massive waterworks.
sentences.zh: 这是一个非常引人注目的例子。

sentences.en: It's a very striking example.
sentences.zh: 新奥尔良的情况极其危险，因为三角洲的性质正在下沉，海平面也在上升。

sentences.en: And New Orleans' situation is extremely precarious because of the nature of the delta, which is sinking, and sea level, which is rising.
sentences.zh: 所以相对海平面是一个巨大的问题。

sentences.en: So relative sea level is a tremendous problem.
sentences.zh: 话虽如此，世界上每个主要沿海城市都将上演某种版本的这种情况。

sentences.en: But that being said, every major coastal city in the world is going to be playing out some version of this.
sentences.zh: 我们愿意在多大程度上搬迁？

sentences.en: To what extent are we going to be willing to move?
sentences.zh: 我们将在多大程度上试图从那些受到海平面上升威胁的地方榨取每一分可能的时间？

sentences.en: And to what extent are we going to try to eke out every possible decade from places that are going to be threatened, increasingly threatened by sea level rise?
sentences.zh: 因为我们已经锁定了实质性的海平面上升。

sentences.en: Because we have already locked in substantial sea level rise.
sentences.zh: 没有人能确切告诉你会有多少。

sentences.en: No one can tell you exactly how much.
sentences.zh: 我们继续排放二氧化碳的时间越长，海平面上升就越严重。

sentences.en: The longer we continue to emit CO2, the more sea level rise we're getting.
sentences.zh: 这是一个非常明确的关系。

sentences.en: That's just a very clear relationship.
sentences.zh: 但请看看名单，每个沿海城市在接下来的本世纪余下时间里都将不得不应对这个问题。

sentences.en: But, you know, just go through the liSt.
sentences.zh: 如果我们因为生活方式的选择和优先事项而永远被锁定在一个干预周期中，我们是否变得更精确了？

sentences.en: Every coastal city is going to be grappling with this over the next, the rest of the century.
sentences.zh: 我们是否学到了什么？

sentences.en: If we're locked into, like, an intervention cycle forever because of our lifestyle choices and our priorities, have we gotten more precise?
sentences.zh: 是的，我认为我们变得知识渊博多了。

sentences.en: Have we gotten, have we learned something?
sentences.zh: 例如，如果有人决定在三角洲土壤上建造新城市，有人会举手说，等一下，

sentences.en: Yes, I think we've gotten a lot more knowledgeable.
sentences.zh: 这是一个问题。

sentences.en: You know, I do think, for example, if someone decided to build, you know, a new city on deltaic soils, you know, someone would raise their hand and say, you know, wait a sec,
sentences.zh: 但这引发了许多新问题，对吧？

sentences.en: this is a problem.
sentences.zh: 所以，所有这些大城市都会提出各种干预措施。

sentences.en: But that raises a lot of new problems, right?
sentences.zh: 例如，他们已经在关注纽约了。

sentences.en: So, you know, there are going to be all these interventions proposed for all these big cities.
sentences.zh: 你打算如何保护纽约？

sentences.en: For example, you know, they're already looking at New York.
sentences.zh: 有很多大规模的可能性。

sentences.en: How are you going to protect New York?
sentences.zh: 人们也会提出很多反对意见，他们理应这样做，关于这些措施会对生态系统、纽约港造成什么影响，

sentences.en: There are lots of massive possibilities.
sentences.zh: 他们将如何把水从一个地方转移到另一个地方，等等。

sentences.en: People are going to raise a lot of objections to them, as well they should, about what they're going to do to, you know, the ecosystem, the New York Harbor,
sentences.zh: 与此同时，海平面正在上升。

sentences.en: how they're going to just place water from one place to another, et cetera, et cetera.
sentences.zh: 所以我并不是说大规模干预是解决之道。

sentences.en: Meanwhile, sea levels are rising, you know.
sentences.zh: 很有可能我们需要采取许多较小的步骤，这些步骤比解决一个巨大的问题更难协调。

sentences.en: So I'm not saying that massive interventions are the way to go.
sentences.zh: 但即使是这些步骤也会遇到阻力。

sentences.en: It's quite possible that we need to take a lot of smaller steps, which are much more difficult to coordinate than a big, massive problem.
sentences.zh: 所以我们处于一个相当复杂的时代和境地，我们的许多价值观将发生冲突，

sentences.en: But those also even, even those run into resistance.
sentences.zh: 既体现在希望社区或城市具有某种自我决定的品质，

sentences.en: So we're in a pretty complicated, you know, time and situation where a lot of our values are going to come into conflict, you know,
sentences.zh: 也体现在无法就我们需要什么干预达成一致。

sentences.en: both in terms of wanting even neighborhoods or cities or whatever to have a sort of a certain self-determining quality,
sentences.zh: 与此同时，水正在蔓延。

sentences.en: but also not being able to agree, you know, on what intervention we need.
sentences.zh: 所以我不知道这会如何发展。

sentences.en: Meanwhile, you know, the water's creeping up.
sentences.zh: 如果它不那么可怕的话，我会觉得这很迷人。

sentences.en: So I don't know how that's going to play out.
sentences.zh: 非常感谢你与我们交谈。

sentences.en: I think it would be fascinating if it, you know, weren't so scary.
sentences.zh: 哦，谢谢你。

sentences.en: Well, thank you so much for talking with us.
